subject: MAP token economics — finops certification for signoff
body:
From: Emma Lin <emma.lin@helixmed.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Sep 2029 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Final MAP + token cost gating question

Rishi —

Thanks for sending the updated MAP. Procurement has reviewed and we're nearly ready to move to legal, but I have a quick finops gating question before we lock the close timeline. On tab 'Unit Cost' your per-100k tokens estimate assumes a 60% hit from prefix caching and an average batch size of 8. For our real-time triage use case (median latency target 150ms), those assumptions are optimistic.

Can you confirm:
- Where the 60% prefix caching number came from (sample traffic or synthetic)?
- Is the batch size distribution modeled as Poisson peaks or steady-state?
- If we need to reduce cache hit to 30% and average batch size to 3, what does the tokens/$ look like and how does that affect estimated monthly cost at our 2M reqs/mo projection?

We need the numbers and a short risk note for our CFO to clear budget before EOW.

—Emma
Head of Procurement, HelixMed

---

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Emma Lin <emma.lin@helixmed.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Sep 2029 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Final MAP + token cost gating question

Emma — thanks, great questions. Short answers up front, details and sensitivity scenarios below. Attaching a finops snapshot and a lightweight batching profile we used for the MAP.

Answers:
- 60% prefix caching: derived from a 7-day sampling exercise on the pilot traffic we saw in July — median prefix reuse was high due to templated triage prompts. We annotated the sampling assumptions in MAP_v3_finops_snapshot.xlsx tab 'Assumptions'.
- Batch size distribution: the MAP used a hybrid model — steady-state batching with opportunistic burst batching during short windows. For modeling we assumed empirical distribution with mean 8 and P(batch >= 12) ~= 9%. See batching_profile_preview.json.
- If cache hit drops to 30% and mean batch size = 3, tokens/$ increases ~2.8x versus MAP baseline. With your 2M reqs/mo projection that pushes the monthly estimate from ~$24k to ~$68k (detailed calc in sheet).

Risk note: If HelixMed requires strict 150ms p95, we recommend a conservative rollout: dedicated capacity (pin vCPU/GPU mix) for the triage route + prefix-KV prefetch for expected templates. That reduces cold-start token costs and keeps tail latency deterministic. I can add a one-paragraph CFO-ready note.

Next steps I propose:
1) I will produce a one-page attachment with 3 sensitivity buckets (optimistic 60% cache/mean batch 8, mid 45%/5, conservative 30%/3) and monthly cost + 12-month run-rate.
2) Neha and Ben — can you confirm if the Dedicated capacity SKU we modeled can meet 150ms p95 at the conservative bucket and whether there are reserved-billing levers to lower unit price?
3) Emma — if that one-pager is good, we can add it to the MAP and circulate to your CFO today.

Rishi
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

---

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Sep 2029 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Final MAP + token cost gating question

Quick tech check — Rishi, I validated the latency/capacity pairing on the conservative bucket. Summary:
- Dedicated g4d.8x with 2 shards gives stable p95 ~140-165ms depending on sequence length and KV hit.
- At cache hit 30% and batch size mean 3, per-token GPU time increases ~2.4x; however prefetching the top-10 templates increases effective reuse to ~38% without impacting latency (prefetch is async).
- Reserved commit (12-month) reduces per-token cost by ~18% in our invoice model; that folds into the monthly numbers you saw.

I can produce a short note on prefetch recommendations and the exact per-token after-reserve pricing.

—Neha
Senior Solutions Engineer

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Sep 2029 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Final MAP + token cost gating question

Adding billing nuance: if HelixMed signs up for 12-month Dedicated commit we can offer a tiered per-embedding/per-token schedule. I ran the conservative bucket through the pricing ladder — with 12-month reserve and 15% volume rebate the monthly cost drops from $68k to ~$52k (still higher than baseline but within CFO tolerance if we show deterministic p95).

I'll draft the CFO paragraph and flag which line items are levers (batching, commit, quantization).

—Ben
Principal FinOps

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Emma Lin <emma.lin@helixmed.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Sep 2029 10:27:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Final MAP + token cost gating question

Emma — attaching the one-pager (copied into the MAP) and a short CFO-ready note below. High-level: three sensitivity buckets with monthly and 12-month run-rate, and the operational levers to keep costs in-line while meeting 150ms p95. Highlights: 1) conservative bucket (30%/3) = $68k/mo, with 12-month commit + 15% rebate moves to $52k/mo; 2) prefetching templates improves effective cache to ~38% without latency hit; 3) Dedicated capacity gives stable tail latency.

CFO note (paste):
"We modeled three finops scenarios tied to caching and batching assumptions. Our baseline (used in MAP) assumes 60% prefix reuse and mean batch size 8 which yields the lowest token/unit cost. To account for HelixMed's real-time constraints we included a conservative sensitivity that assumes 30% cache and mean batch 3 — this raises the monthly run-rate from $24k to $68k. The organisation can mitigate the downside by committing to a 12-month dedicated reservation and enabling template prefetch; combined these reduce expected cost to ~$52k/mo while maintaining a p95 latency target of ~150ms. Key levers for HelixMed: negotiate a 12-month commit, enable KV prefetch for top templates, and consider quantized model variant for lower-cost bulk cases."
If you'd like, I can convert that into a single-slide summary for your CFO.

Rishi

Attachments: MAP_v3_finops_snapshot.xlsx (spreadsheet), batching_profile_preview.json (config), latency_summary_screenshot.png (image)
